subject: geography
chapter_title: Solar Radiation, Heat Balance and Temperature

concepts.title: Insolation, Heat Budget and Albedo
concepts.definition: Insolation is the incoming solar radiation received at the top of the atmosphere, of which about 35 units are reflected back by clouds, dust and surfaces as albedo, and the balance heats the land, water and air, so the earth maintains a heat budget of gains equal to losses.
concepts.key_idea: The earth as a whole neither warms nor cools because the incoming shortwave radiation balances the outgoing longwave terrestrial radiation.

concepts.title: Temperature Distribution and Its Controlling Factors
concepts.definition: Temperature distribution over the globe follows latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, ocean currents, air masses and slope aspects, and is shown by isotherms that bend across continents and oceans between January and July.
concepts.key_idea: Isotherms generally run east-west but deviate over land and sea, showing higher temperatures over continents in summer and lower in winter at the same latitude.

concepts.title: Latitudinal Heat Balance and Its Global Effects
concepts.definition: The latitudinal heat balance shows surplus net radiation between the tropics and deficit towards the poles, and atmospheric and oceanic circulation transfer the surplus heat polewards, keeping the tropics from overheating and the poles from freezing.
concepts.key_idea: Without this poleward heat transport by winds and currents, the equator would grow steadily hotter and high latitudes steadily colder.
